card.summary: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, subjecting them to the same regulatory controls and criminal penalties as fentanyl analogues. It also creates alternative and expedited registration processes for certain schedule I research involving these substances, modifies research site and personnel requirements, and outlines rules for manufacturing small quantities for research purposes.

summary: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, subjecting them to the same quantity thresholds and criminal penalties as fentanyl analogues. It also creates a new alternative registration process for certain schedule I research and adjusts various research requirements under the Controlled Substances Act.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to the same quantity thresholds and penalties as offenses involving fentanyl analogues, such as a 10-year mandatory minimum prison term for 100 grams or more.
affected_groups.group: Individuals involved in offenses with fentanyl-related substances

affected_groups.effect: Subject to modified registration processes, site rules, inspection waivers, and allowances for small-scale manufacturing associated with schedule I substance research.

key_provisions: Permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act.
Applies the same quantity thresholds and criminal penalties for offenses involving fentanyl-related substances as those involving fentanyl analogues.
Establishes a new, alternative registration process for certain schedule I research by practitioners.
Permits a single registration for related research sites under specific circumstances and waives new inspection requirements in certain situations.
Allows registered researchers to perform certain small-scale manufacturing activities coincident to research without obtaining a separate manufacturing registration.
Expresses the sense of Congress agreeing with the court interpretation in United States v. McCray regarding controlled substance analogues.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact economic cost or budget allocation for implementing the new registration and enforcement procedures.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, subjecting them to the same quantity thresholds and criminal penalties as fentanyl analogues. It also creates a new alternative registration process for certain schedule I research and adjusts various research requirements under the Controlled Substances Act.
summary_detail.significance: This law permanently alters how fentanyl-related substances are classified and penalized under federal drug laws, while streamlining certain administrative and registration requirements for scientific and medical researchers studying these substances.
